question.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t}-t\,,\frac{1}{t}+t\,⟩$ at the point $P(0,2),$ valid for all real values of $u?$

current_example.problem: Find a parametrization of the tangent line to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \cos{t}, \: \sin{t},\: 4t^2\right\rangle$ at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let  $P$ be the point at the tip of the vector $\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right ).$  At this point,  the vector $\mathbf r'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right )$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
\mathbf R(u)=\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right )+u \, \mathbf r'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right ), \qquad u \in (-\infty, \infty).
$$

 

First, we find $\mathbf r\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,4{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}⟩=⟨0,1,{\pi }^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,8t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,8(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,4\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the given curve at the point $P$ where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(u)=⟨0,1,{\pi }^{2}⟩+u⟨-1,0,4\pi ⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
